title: Interop kickoff: SDK & function design - TeraHealth POC scoping
summary: Kickoff for a 4-week pilot to validate Redwood's OpenAI-compatible SDK integration, function/tool calling, structured output, and benchmark targets. Agreed success criteria: p95 latency < 300ms for 512-token responses, cost < $0.002/token equivalent at target QPS, end-to-end throughput 120 reqs/min with 8 concurrent workers. Security requirements (SOC2, KMS, VPC) and a scrubbed dataset for benchmarking were confirmed. Next: deliver benchmark harness, sample integration guide, schedule infra access and a canary test in week 2.

Meeting header:
- Date: 2027-04-14
- Time: 17:00 UTC
- Duration: 58 minutes
- Attendees: Lena Patel (Redwood AE), Marco Ruiz (Redwood SE), Jing Wei (Redwood SE), Dr. Aaron Blake (TeraHealth CTO), Maya Fernandez (ML Eng), Sanjay Rao (Infra), Priya Menon (Security)

Optional auto sections:
Summary: see summary field above

Transcript:
[00:00] Lena Patel: Okay everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intros, then we'll jump into the POC scope. Marco and Jing from our side will cover the benchmark plan and the SDK/compat approach.
[00:18] Dr. Aaron Blake: Thanks Lena. From TeraHealth side we want to validate both latency and deterministic structured output for our clinical summarization use case. Maya and Sanjay are here to cover model integration and infra.
[00:30] Marco Ruiz: Hi all, quick note — we'll propose an OpenAI-compatible endpoint pattern so you can swap in our hosted or your private deployment later. The goal for the pilot: confirm end-to-end latency, throughput, and structured JSON output reliability when using tool/function calls.
[00:46] Maya Fernandez: We have a dataset of clinical notes, avg token length around 420, some long ones to 2k. We'll sanitize and provide a sample. Our main success criteria: the structured output must include consistent fields: diagnosis_code, summary_text, severity_score (0-5), follow_up_actions array.
[01:10] Jing Wei: Perfect. For structured output we'll use Redwood's structured output schema enforcement plus a small eval harness that asserts field presence and type. We can run both model-level checks and end-to-end checks after function/tool calling.
[01:35] Sanjay Rao: Infrastructure constraints — we need VPC deployment or dedicated instances due to PHI. We also need KMS integration and audit logs. Latency SLOs are secondary to compliance but still important.
[01:50] Lena Patel: Understood. We support Private/VPC + KMS + audit logs. For the pilot we usually do a private control plane with a customer-managed VPC peering, or we can spin a dedicated reserved pool if you prefer faster ramp.
[02:08] Dr. Aaron Blake: Cost sensitivity is real — we have a target of keeping inference cost below an equivalent of $0.002 per token at 512-token median output, else we'll need to look at quantization or a smaller model.
[02:26] Marco Ruiz: We'll include quantized variants and measure quality regressions with our eval set. Typical approach: baseline with fp16, then 4-bit quant run for cost-limited pass and measure ROUGE/F1 drop.
[02:45] Priya Menon: On security, SOC2 compliance and SSO (SAML) for console access are musts. Also need a retention policy — logs for 90 days and an option for 365 on request.
[03:00] Lena Patel: We can enable long-retention add-ons, SSO SAML is supported, and we provide audit logs and customer-controlled KMS. We'll include our security brief after the call.
[03:12] Maya Fernandez: Great. Can we next agree on the benchmark dimensions? What do you need from us to size the workload?
[03:23] Marco Ruiz: Good question. We'll ask for: (1) sample of 200-500 sanitized transcripts representative of short/long tails; (2) concurrency target (how many concurrent requests you'd expect in production); (3) expected QPS or requests per minute during peak windows; (4) token distribution histogram.
[03:45] Dr. Aaron Blake: For MVP, target concurrency is 8 workers, expected peak 120 reqs/min, some scheduled batch windows overnight at higher volume.
[03:58] Marco Ruiz: Ok that's helpful. We'll design bench harness to run synthetic concurrency up to 12 to test headroom and fallback policies. We'll measure p50/p95/p99 latency and throughput, cost per token, and structured-output accuracy measured as schema pass rate and key-value field validation.
[04:25] Jing Wei: We'll also instrument KV cache hits for repeated prefixes — a lot of your notes will share templates. That can drop token costs significantly. We'll include cache-hitting scenarios in the benchmark.
[04:40] Maya Fernandez: Triage question — do you support function calling that returns structured objects we can ingest directly? We want to avoid postprocessing whenever possible.
[04:52] Marco Ruiz: Yes, Redwood supports OpenAI-style function calling and SDK wrappers that deserialize function responses into typed objects. We can demonstrate that in a mini-demo. There are edge cases when models hallucinate types — the eval harness will catch those.
[05:08] Dr. Aaron Blake: Timeline — we have two-month budget window for pilot evaluation. What would your recommended pilot schedule look like?
[05:20] Lena Patel: Our standard pilot is 4 weeks: week 0 (kickoff and infra prep), week 1 baseline benchmarks + SDK integration, week 2 canary with private/VPC or dedicated pool and function-calling flows, week 3 quality tuning and repeat benchmarks, week 4 sign-off and next-step recommendations. If you need two months we'll spread it out, but we usually get meaningful diffs in 3-4 weeks.
[05:43] Sanjay Rao: For infra prep we need a list of IPs, egress rules and a minimal IAM policy. Also we'll need a short maintenance window for peering.
[05:55] Jing Wei: We'll provide a network checklist and a one-click terraform snippet for VPC peering. Also a runbook for starting dedicated pools if you prefer.
[06:10] Priya Menon: Please send your SOC2 cert and pen test summary. Also need an optional data processing addendum — our legal team will review.
[06:22] Lena Patel: We'll share the security pack (SOC2, ISO scope, pen tests) and our DPA template.
[06:30] Maya Fernandez: Can you describe how the SDK maps to our current OpenAI-based integration? We have a microservice that hits openai.com/v1/chat/completions today.
[06:41] Marco Ruiz: The SDK exposes an OpenAI-compatible HTTP path and SDK bindings in Python/Node. Endpoints and payloads are the same for messages+functions; we add optional headers for routing, quant profiles, and can attach a model_alias to map to a quantized runtime. So minimal code change for you.
[07:00] Maya Fernandez: Any gotchas with KV cache or streaming?
[07:05] Jing Wei: Streaming will work with the same socket semantics; KV cache requires a small client-side change to pass session ids so the runtime can stitch state. We have examples.
[07:18] Dr. Aaron Blake: Benchmarks — we need both synthetic load and realistic latency for long sequences. For long notes (1-2k tokens) p95 at 1s is acceptable, but for standard notes (<=512 tokens) we want p95 < 300ms. Can you realistically hit that on a private deployment?
[07:40] Marco Ruiz: On dedicated A100-like instances with batching tuned for median 512 tokens, p95 < 300ms is achievable. For private on-prem we need to match kernel optimizations; we'll run an initial benchmark to confirm.
[07:58] Sanjay Rao: If we choose private on-prem, what's your recommended hardware? Cost vs perf tradeoff?
[08:05] Marco Ruiz: For predictable low latency at scale, 80GB GPUs or their latest equivalents with NVLink are recommended. For cost-constrained pilots we can use 48GB with model sharding and quantization. We'll include a hardware recommendation matrix.
[08:23] Maya Fernandez: How will you measure accuracy degradation when moving to 4-bit quant? We can't compromise on clinical correctness.
[08:30] Jing Wei: We'll run a differential eval: same prompts on fp16 baseline and on quantized run, then compute span-level F1 and key-value exact match for structured fields. We'll flag every regression > 2% and provide example failure cases.
[08:50] Dr. Aaron Blake: Good. Also include a human-in-the-loop annotation round for critical cases.
[08:56] Marco Ruiz: Will do. We'll propose a small human eval panel for the top 100 failure cases.
[09:05] Priya Menon: Data residency — we must ensure that any hosted logs with PHI remain in our chosen region. Can you restrict region?
[09:15] Lena Patel: Yes, we have region pinning for data and private control plane options so logs and KV stores remain in your region. We'll outline the options and tradeoffs.
[09:27] Maya Fernandez: Sample data delivery — when can we send sanitized dataset?
[09:31] Dr. Aaron Blake: We'll target end of this week; Maya will scrub and drop to a secure S3 bucket, share role-based access.
[09:40] Marco Ruiz: Great. For benchmarking we'll need a manifest with token counts and labels for gold structured outputs.
[09:47] Maya Fernandez: We'll produce that. Expect ~500 samples for the pilot.
[09:52] Sanjay Rao: Network: we need the peering CIDR and connection doc.
[09:56] Jing Wei: We'll send the terraform snippet and a step-by-step.
[10:01] Lena Patel: Let's talk deliverables and next steps.
[10:05] Marco Ruiz: Deliverables from Redwood: (1) benchmark harness and instructions; (2) OpenAI-compatible SDK quickstart and code snippets; (3) security pack; (4) hardware recommendation; (5) an eval report template. We'll also run an initial smoke test to validate connectivity.
[10:23] Dr. Aaron Blake: And deliverables from TeraHealth: sanitized sample set + manifest, infra access for peering, list of key success stakeholders and sign-off criteria.
[10:34] Maya Fernandez: One more thing — could you include a sample function schema we can adopt for the diagnostics extraction? Something typed we can version.
[10:42] Jing Wei: Yes, we'll include a versioned function schema example and an OpenAPI snippet to wire into your microservice.
[10:49] Priya Menon: Legal: send DPA and a high-level SOC2 scope. We'll loop in legal and security for review.
[10:55] Lena Patel: To avoid confusion, summarizing next steps now.
[10:59] Marco Ruiz: I'll run through the technical checklist: - send bench harness repo link - terraform VPC snippet - sample function schema - SDK quickstart demos with function calling example (Python + Node)
[11:19] Dr. Aaron Blake: We'll: - provide sanitized dataset and manifest by EOW - provide infra contact for peering - assign sign-off stakeholders
[11:30] Lena Patel: Any other blockers?
[11:33] Maya Fernandez: Not for now. We'll review security pack once you share.
[11:37] Sanjay Rao: Need to slot a 2-hour window for week 2 canary, preference Fri night for lower traffic.
[11:44] Marco Ruiz: We'll accommodate that and propose two possible time slots in the calendar invite.
[11:50] Priya Menon: Also request that access tokens used for the benchmark have least privilege and auto-expire.
[11:55] Jing Wei: Agreed — we provide scoped bench credentials and rotation guidance.
[12:00] Lena Patel: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the links and action items.
[12:05] Dr. Aaron Blake: Thanks, talk soon.

End of transcript.
